gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much taller a full-height board sits at the wrist edge. Without keycaps, Keychron's figures put the front edge of the Q1 Max at 22.6 mm and the low-profile K3 Max at 11 mm. That is 11.6 mm higher, or 2.05×. The Q1 Max also weighs 3.3× as much (1,724 g vs 525 g) and costs $120 more at Keychron's own store today.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches, and both chats list zero results and zero cited pages. So there were no rival pages to compare against, and the answer itself is the only competition. It says only 'less wrist extension' and 'may benefit from a wrist rest', with no height, weight or price gap in numbers. The figures here put a size on that claim, but they don't overturn its conclusion.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's lean for laptop and desk typists. The low-profile K3 Max starts 11.6 mm lower at the front edge, 1.16 lb against 3.80 lb, and $89.99 against $209.99. That is why the full-height Q1 Max needs a wrist rest and the K3 Max mostly doesn't. On rear height without keycaps the difference grows to 20.8 mm (35.8 vs 15). The Q1 Max is the pick only if the shopper wants full-height keycaps and switch choice and doesn't mind a wrist rest. Lofree's Flow84 claims a 10 mm thickness, which fits the same low-profile range.
